勅.meaning: A messenger who is all <part>muscle</part> sprints through every village with a <part>bundle</part> of scrolls on his back, nailing one to each door: 'From today, all cats must be called Your Majesty.' Nobody argues with an <kanji>imperial order</kanji>.
勅.on: The palace pays him in bars of <sound>choc</sound>olate.
勅.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat reads it aloud to a <sound>ko</sound>ala, who drops his <sound>to</sound>ffee, ties a <sound>kno</sound>t in his scarf and runs off to tell the fish on the <sound>ree</sound>f.

斑.meaning: A <part>dancer</part> twirls between two <part>king</part> twins as they paint the ballroom, one in red and one in yellow. Every spin flicks paint off her skirt onto the walls, the floor and the kings' beards. By the end, the whole palace is <kanji>mottled</kanji>.
斑.on: A bee flies in and mistakes the yellow spots for <sound>hon</sound>ey.
斑.kun: The dancer flops down, dizzy, on a spotty <sound>fu</sound>ton.

玩.meaning: A grumpy <part>king</part> won't sign any laws until his carpenter brings him a <part>sawhorse</part> with a painted head and a mop for a tail. He gallops it round the throne room, neighing, all afternoon. The court calls it the royal steed. It's a <kanji>toy</kanji>.
玩.on: Its legs get clogged with <sound>gun</sound>k from the castle moat.
玩.kun: He polishes it with a <sound>mo</sound>p, feeds it <sound>chee</sound>se, sighs '<sound>Ah</sound>,' and tucks it in on the <sound>so</sound>fa.

嗣.meaning: The old <part>director</part> of a puppet theatre retires. Instead of passing his plays to his son, he tucks the <part>scroll</part> of every script into the wooden <part>mouth</part> of his favourite puppet, a grumpy owl. The owl clacks its beak and takes a bow: the theatre's new <kanji>heir</kanji>.
嗣.on: On opening night the owl hides behind a painted <sound>shi</sound>eld and recites every line from memory.

恣.meaning: At the ice cream van, the girl at the window calls '<part>next</part>!', but the man at the front never moves. He just orders another scoop for himself, then another, until he holds a tower topped with a cone shaped like a <part>heart</part>, all his. The whole queue groans: how <kanji>selfish</kanji>.
恣.on: When a little dog begs for a lick, he blocks the cone with a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
恣.kun: He <sound>ho</sound>gs the only bench, sprawled on a <sound>shee</sound>pskin, and <sound>mu</sound>nches, <sound>mu</sound>ttering 'mine', just as he pleases.

壱.meaning: A <part>gentleman</part> in a top hat goes camping with exactly one thing: a silver <part>spoon</part>, which he tucks under a tiny <part>blanket</part> each night. Asked how many spoons he packed, he lifts one gloved finger and answers in his poshest voice: 'Precisely one.' That's <kanji>one (formal)</kanji>.
壱.on: At sunrise he paints the spoon on an <sound>ea</sound>sel, while a curious <sound>chee</sound>tah peeks at the lonely canvas.
壱.kun: He sleeps with his <sound>hee</sound>ls against a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, then wakes and sneezes once, very politely: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

訃.meaning: The town's oldest <part>faucet</part> drips its last drop after a hundred years. The mayor gives a teary <part>speech</part> beside it, and next morning the paper prints half a page about its long, leaky life, with a photo of it in its prime: the faucet's <kanji>obituary</kanji>.
訃.on: Its worn-out washer is laid to rest on a tiny rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton.
訃.kun: The paper girl reads it, and <sound>she</sound> <sound>ru</sound>shes off to <sound>se</sound>nd the sad news to every door on the street.

畏.meaning: Over a <part>rice field</part>, a <part>garment</part> floats up all by itself: a huge golden robe, arms spread wide, with <part>one</part> stiff belt across its middle. The frogs stop croaking, the farmer drops his hoe, and the whole valley stares up, speechless with <kanji>awe</kanji>.
畏.on: Even an <sound>ee</sound>l pokes its head out of the mud to gape at it.
畏.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm <sound>shee</sound>pdog bows low before the robe, a <sound>co</sound>conut balanced on its head: respectfully.

附.meaning: A goat on a mountain keeps eating every flag the climbers plant. So the last climber finds a way to <part>attach</part> her <part>pennant</part> to the goat's own horn with tape, glue and three knots. Now the summit flag wanders the mountain all day, firmly <kanji>affixed</kanji>.
附.on: At night the goat curls up on a rolled-out <sound>fu</sound>ton, the flag still waving over its head.
附.kun: A <sound>tsu</sound>nami of wind roars up the slope, and the flag still clings on.

但.meaning: A hotel hangs a sign on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door: 'Free breakfast for all!' Below, in tiny letters: 'Served only before <part>daybreak</part>.' Guests stagger down at four in their pyjamas, grumbling about that one little <kanji>however</kanji>.
但.on: The kitchen is reached through a long, dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, so they bump into each other with their trays.
但.kun: At the end of the tunnel, a <sound>tu</sound>gboat captain and his pet <sound>du</sound>ck have already eaten everything: they read the small print first.

煎.meaning: A penguin chef stands <part>in front</part> of a grill of glowing <part>hot coals</part>, flipping fish with his flippers. He keeps leaning closer for a better look, until his own bow tie starts to smoke. He's learning the hard way how to <kanji>broil</kanji>.
煎.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try walrus stands by with a bucket of snow in case the chef catches fire.
煎.kun: After dinner the penguin boils seaweed into a dark, bitter brew and sells it for one <sound>cen</sound>t a cup: to brew by boiling.

哺.meaning: A mother hedgehog lies in the barn while her babies drink, each tiny <part>mouth</part> busy. The farmer's cat stands guard with a <part>flyswatter</part>, whacking every fly that buzzes near. Nobody disturbs a hedgehog while she's trying to <kanji>nurse</kanji>.
哺.on: When the babies finally sleep, the cat rewards itself with a <sound>ho</sound>tdog.
哺.kun: Years later the grown hedgehogs give the cat a <sound>hug</sound> and a <sound>cu</sound>shion of soft hay: it helped raise them.

且.meaning: A pushy peddler on a night train holds up a lamp shaped like the <part>moon</part>. 'It glows! It hums!' Then he always has <part>one</part> more thing to add: a stand, a spare bulb, a free bag. Nobody needs them, but nobody can say no to his favourite word, <kanji>moreover</kanji>.
且.on: He sells it all from a tiny <sound>sho</sound>p in the last carriage, so short a stop the doors slam shut mid-sale.
且.kun: And he throws in a free <sound>cu</sound>p of tea as well.

𠮟.meaning: Every morning at <part>seven</part>, a cuckoo bursts out of the clock in the hall, opens its little wooden <part>mouth</part> and yells at the family: shoes on the stairs! Crumbs on the table! Even the dog gets told off. This clock doesn't cuckoo, it likes to <kanji>scold</kanji>.
𠮟.on: The family hides under a big bed <sound>sheet</sound>, but it shouts through that too.
𠮟.kun: Then Grandma scolds it right back: <sound>she</sound> <sound>cu</sound>ts it off mid-squawk with one firm 'Enough!'

弐.meaning: A butler sets up a croquet lawn, hammering in a <part>stake</part> and laying <part>two</part> polished mallets beside it. 'How many players, madam?' The duchess raises two gloved fingers: 'Two, if you please.' That is <kanji>two (formal)</kanji>.
弐.on: She keeps score by poking tiny holes in a card with a <sound>nee</sound>dle.
弐.kun: Between shots, the duchess cools one <sound>foo</sound>t in a <sound>tu</sound>b of iced tea.
